# The Traveler Who Returns

## Scripture

*"But ask the animals, and they will teach you, or the birds in the sky, and they will tell you; or speak to the earth, and it will teach you, or let the fish in the sea inform you. Which of all these does not know that the hand of the Lord has done this?"* — Job 12:7-9

## Reflection

In the fall sky, look for a fuzzy patch of light in the constellation Andromeda. That faint glow is the Great Andromeda Galaxy—the most distant thing visible to the naked eye, nearly 2.5 million light-years away. Yet it is also the closest major galaxy to our own, a neighbor among the stars.

Even more remarkable: Andromeda is traveling toward us, slowly closing the vast distance across deep space. Two great islands of light, separated by eons, moving toward one another in a patient, cosmic embrace.

Job reminds us that creation itself testifies to the hand of God. The heavens do not merely exist; they *speak*. And what they speak of is a God who draws near—who does not remain distant but moves toward His people. Like Andromeda crossing the dark, God approaches us across every expanse of our wandering and doubt.

In this autumn season, when the earth tilts and the nights lengthen, remember: distance is never the final word with God. He is the Traveler who returns, the Light that comes close. What seems impossibly far—peace, hope, a healing you've waited years for—may already be crossing the dark toward you.

## Prayer

Lord of the galaxies, thank You for drawing near. When You feel far, remind me that You are always moving toward me. Give me patient hope in the waiting. Amen.
